chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Ishaq, from Fayd, from Ash'ath, from Shurayh, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about a slave who was sold while he had a debt upon him; he said: 'His debt is upon the one who permitted him to trade and consumed its price.'
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for the debt of a slave who was sold after trading?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of vicarious liability in Islamic commercial law, where the master bears the debt of a slave who traded with permission, provided the master consumed the profits. This ruling underscores the concept of *ikhtiyar* (choice/permission), linking the right to profit with the burden of debt, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence regarding *mudabbad* (slaves with autonomy). It serves as a foundational precedent for modern applications of agency and profit-sharing models in fiqh.
